gloss: reversal; relapse; going back to an earlier state

definitions.explanation: Returning to a previous or worse state after progress had been made. Used for situations, conditions, and processes that move backward.

examples.japanese: {景気|けいき}が{逆戻|ぎゃくもど}りした。
{交渉|こうしょう}が{振|ふ}り{出|だ}しに{逆戻|ぎゃくもど}りしてしまった。
examples.english: The negotiations went right back to square one.

examples.japanese: せっかく{体重|たいじゅう}を{落|お}としたのに、{食|た}べ{過|す}ぎて{逆戻|ぎゃくもど}りしてしまった。
examples.english: I finally lost the weight, but I overate and it all came back.

notes:
USAGE:
{逆戻|ぎゃくもど}り conveys the frustration of losing progress. It implies that effort was made but the situation has returned to where it started — or worse.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {逆戻|ぎゃくもど}りする (to go backward, to relapse)
- {振|ふ}り{出|だ}しに{逆戻|ぎゃくもど}り (back to square one)
- {元|もと}に{逆戻|ぎゃくもど}りする (to revert to the original state)

GRAMMAR:
Used as a noun or with する to form an intransitive verb.
